title: Build: URL shortener service
summary: Multi-process service on localhost: a durable log-structured store, an API with idempotent creates, a redirect cache with negative caching and stampede protection, a per-client rate limiter, failure injection, and an open-loop p99 report.

units.title: The durable store: an append-only log, crash recovery and a store process
The API and the redirect cache: idempotent creates, negative caching, stampedes, invalidation across instances
Limits, failure injection and the p99 report

labs.title: The service: append-only checksummed log with crash recovery, store and api processes, idempotent creates, LRU+TTL redirect cache with negative caching, singleflight and stale-if-error, per-client token bucket, deadline budgets, graceful drain; multi-process failure-injection tests
Open-loop load generator with intended-start latency (coordinated omission), nearest-rank percentiles and a p50/p95/p99 report

outcomes.text: Write a design-rationale document for a multi-process service before building it, with per-component failure predictions, and revise it against what failure injection actually showed.

Implement an append-only, checksummed log with an in-memory index, an fsync policy and crash recovery that truncates a torn tail but refuses to open on mid-file corruption, and explain why SIGKILL cannot test fsync.
Expose the log as a store process with insert-if-absent, and explain why that one atomic primitive lets several API instances allocate random codes and claim idempotency keys without coordinating.

Implement an idempotent create with a stored intent record that any retry can roll forward, with the right status for replay (201 + Idempotent-Replayed), reuse with a different body (422) and concurrent duplicates.
Design the redirect hot path: 302 with explicit Cache-Control, 404 vs 410 with tombstones, an LRU+TTL cache with negative entries, singleflight on a detached context, and serve-time expiry checks.
Close the invalidation race between a delete and an in-flight cache fill, and state (and measure) the staleness bound for other instances when invalidation is local.

Implement a per-client token-bucket limiter with bounded memory and truthful Retry-After, place it before any expensive work, and compute what a per-instance limit really admits behind a load balancer.
Apply deadline budgets, stale-if-error and fast 503 + Retry-After so the service degrades predictably when the store is down, slow or partitioned, and drain in-flight requests on SIGTERM.
Inject failures across processes (SIGKILL, SIGTERM under load, latency, blackhole, refused connections, torn and corrupt files) and turn each prediction into a deterministic test.
Build an open-loop load generator that measures from the intended start, report p50/p95/p99 with nearest-rank percentiles, and explain how coordinated omission hides a stall.
